pattern: Broadcast to a huge audience: write once to a log, route per server (not per viewer) through pub/sub, and cap what each viewer receives by batching and sampling so delivery cost depends on audience size, not on write rate.

tips.nudge: What does a viewer do besides watch?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for adding a comment to a live video.
tips.show: F1: Viewers post a short comment (≤ 200 characters) on a live video.

tips.nudge: What makes these comments different from comments under a recorded video?
tips.hint: Capture that viewers see each other's comments while the stream is on.
tips.show: F2: Viewers of a live video see other viewers' new comments in real time.

tips.nudge: You open a stream that started an hour ago. What is on screen?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for what a joiner sees, and whether comments outlive the stream.
tips.show: F3: A late joiner sees the last ~50 comments at once; comments are kept for replay with the recording.

tips.nudge: How old can a comment be before the conversation stops making sense next to the video?
tips.hint: State a post → screen latency target.
tips.show: N1: A comment appears on other viewers' screens within 2 s at p99.

tips.nudge: Averages hide the event everyone remembers. Which one?
tips.hint: Name the biggest single stream you must support and its comment rate.
tips.show: N2: One video may have 5M concurrent viewers and 10k comments/s without slowing other videos.

tips.nudge: How often does a watching viewer comment?
tips.hint: concurrent viewers ÷ seconds between comments per viewer.
tips.show: comments_peak = 20M / 600 s ≈ 33k /s (hot video alone ≈ 10k /s).

tips.nudge: How many open connections does the read side hold at peak?
tips.hint: Write the concurrent viewer count down, and the size of the biggest single stream.
tips.show: concurrent_viewers = 20M; hot_viewers = 5M; at 100k connections per gateway ≈ 200 gateways.

tips.nudge: Each comment has to reach how many screens?
tips.hint: Multiply viewers by comments per second for the hot video, then compare with sending a batch twice a second.
tips.show: naive: 5M × 10k = 5 × 10^10 /s (impossible); batched: 20M × 2 = 40M /s (~80 GB/s at 2 KB per batch).

tips.nudge: What does the app call when the viewer taps send?
tips.hint: A POST on the video's comments with a client-generated id for retries.
tips.show: POST /videos/{id}/comments {client_comment_id, text} → 201 {comment_id, ts}

tips.nudge: How does the app receive comments it didn't ask for one by one?
tips.hint: A long-lived GET the server writes events into, plus something for the joiner's first screen.
tips.show: GET /videos/{id}/comments/stream (SSE: batch, delete events); GET /videos/{id}/comments/recent?limit=50

tips.nudge: What do you store for each comment, and how is it read back for a replay?
tips.hint: Partition by video, order by time.
tips.show: comments(video_id + hour bucket PK, comment_id time-ordered CK, user_id, text, status, ts) in Cassandra.

checks.label: Accepting and keeping comments designed as a part

tips.nudge: A posted comment has to be stored and shown. What if those two disagree?
tips.hint: Add a part for the write path: compare SQL + polling, database-then-publish, and appending to a log both sides consume.
tips.show: Part 'Comment ingestion': append to Kafka keyed by video_id and ack; persisters batch-insert into Cassandra; dispatchers read the same log.

checks.label: Getting comments onto screens designed as a part

tips.nudge: 20M viewers on hundreds of servers. How does a comment find its viewers?
tips.hint: Add a part for delivery: compare CDN polling, per-viewer routing, and gateways subscribing per video.
tips.show: Part 'Real-time delivery': SSE gateways subscribe once per video to a Redis pub/sub channel and fan out in memory.

checks.label: The biggest stream designed as a part

tips.nudge: 5M viewers × 10k comments/s. Can anyone read that? Should you send it?
tips.hint: Add a part for the hot stream: compare delivering everything, client-side dropping, rooms, and server-side batching + sampling.
tips.show: Part 'Hot stream': dispatchers batch every 500 ms and sample to ~10 comments per batch; deliveries = viewers × 2 /s.

checks.label: First screen for joiners designed as a part

tips.nudge: A million people open the same stream in a minute. What do they all ask for?
tips.hint: Add a part for the joiner's first screen: compare database reads, an in-memory list, and an edge cache in front.
tips.show: Part 'Recent comments': a 50-item Redis list per video maintained by dispatchers, served through the CDN with a 1 s TTL.

tips.nudge: Polling 20M clients every second is 20M requests/s. What lets the server speak first?
tips.hint: A fleet whose only job is holding long-lived connections.
tips.show: Comment gateways ×200 (SSE, ~100k connections each) behind the load balancer.

checks.label: Comments routed to the servers that need them

tips.nudge: A comment on video X must reach only the gateways that have viewers of X.
tips.hint: Something gateways subscribe to, keyed by video.
tips.show: Redis pub/sub channel video:{id}; each gateway subscribes once per video it serves.

tips.nudge: Should the POST wait until 5M screens have the comment?
tips.hint: Ack after one durable write; everything else consumes asynchronously.
tips.show: Comment service → Kafka (key = video_id) → persisters and dispatchers.

checks.label: Order of comments on screen decided

tips.nudge: Two viewers see the same two comments. Must they appear in the same order?
tips.hint: Decide who assigns the order and at what scope.
tips.show: Order per video by Kafka partition offset (time-ordered ids for replay); no global order needed.

tips.nudge: A slur is posted on a 5M-viewer stream. Where is it stopped, and how is it taken back?
tips.hint: Decide what is filtered at post time and how a delete reaches screens that already show it.
tips.show: Blocked-word filter in the comment service before the log; deletes are tombstone events on the same live path; recent list and storage apply them.

tips.nudge: Which resource runs out first during a World Cup final?
tips.hint: Walk the read path for the hottest video.
tips.show: Gateway egress (~80 GB/s), the hot video's single partition and dispatcher, the hot recent-comments key (CDN in front).

tips.nudge: How would you know comments are arriving 10 s late on one stream?
tips.hint: Measure end to end, per video.
tips.show: Post → screen p99, comments/s and viewers per video, sampling ratio, gateway egress, consumer lag, CDN hit ratio.
